Paszab Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Paszab, Hungary

Not demolished. Paszab's Jewish community, formed in the late 18th century, joined the Orthodox stream following the 1869 Schism in Hungarian Jewry; population grew from 25 in 1820 to 71 by 1910, falling to 55 by 1944. In the 1940s, Rabbi Ede Fried of neighboring Tiszabercel led local religious life before he and most of his congregation were murdered at Auschwitz. Immediately after Passover 1944, following German occupation, all local Jews were sent to the severely overcrowded Nyíregyháza Ghetto, then deported to Auschwitz within weeks. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with its latest confirmed tombstone dated 1901 (though later burials may have occurred unrecorded). The Heritage Foundation for Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries restored and fenced the site in 2011.
